Goldman Sachs' candidates discuss credit exposure from OTC derivative counterpart defaults and Russia-related exposures. These specific credit risk events/geographies are not comparable to BAC's disclosure on broad commercial portfolio industry concentrations and committed exposure volumes.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, nonperforming exposure increased by $2.3 billion, predominantly driven by the Real Estate sector, specifically concentrated in Office, Healthcare, and Consumer & Retail segments, resulting from downgrades.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose changes in credit exposure concentrations driven by sector-specific downgrades. BAC reports that its total commercial committed exposure growth was concentrated in Asset managers, Finance companies, and Individuals, reaching $1.3 trillion. In contrast, JPM highlights that its nonperforming exposure increased significantly by $2.3 billion, predominantly driven by the Real Estate sector (Office, Healthcare, and Consumer & Retail) due to downgrades, indicating a specific deterioration in credit quality within that concentrated sector rather than the broad volume growth seen in BAC.

sentences.text: Total commercial committed exposure increased $72.5 billion during 2024 to $1.3 trillion.
The increase in commercial committed exposure was concentrated in Asset managers and funds, Finance companies and Individuals and trusts.

As of December 31, 2024, nonperforming exposure increased by $2.3 billion, predominantly driven by Real Estate, concentrated in Office, Healthcare and Consumer & Retail, in each case resulting from downgrades.

comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Real Estate Lending Exposure and Amounts
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, lending against commercial real estate properties totaled $10.7 billion and $9.4 billion, respectively, representing 4.4% and 4.5% of total exposure in the Institutional Securities segment.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose specific commercial credit exposure amounts and concentrations, though BAC provides broad aggregate commercial exposure while MS details Commercial Real Estate (CRE) lending. BAC states total commercial committed exposure increased to $1.3 trillion, with Asset managers and funds being a primary area of concentration. MS reports that its lending against commercial real estate properties totaled $10.7 billion, representing 4.4% of total exposure in its Institutional Securities segment. While BAC highlights growth in finance and asset management sectors, MS isolates CRE lending volume and its proportion to total segment exposure.
